memory_before.meridian-credits/release-1.0-credit-agre:
Meridian Credits release "1.0" loyalty credit agreement (Finance-approved; source: issue trial-896 description). Applies to every consumer of release 1.0 (single-line quote and full-statement total). Release "1.0" is the initial agreement; an omitted request release selects the current agreement, an explicit supported release selects that version, and versions introduced in an issue stay supported afterward. Public suites send explicit release values, so an earlier-release suite stays valid when the current agreement changes.

Charge line: exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id (nonempty strings; line_id unique per request), service_on (YYYY-MM-DD, 2020-01-01..2099-12-31, never excludes a line), charge_cents (nonnegative integer US cents). Subscription identity is the pair (account_id, subscription_id); a subscription may have several lines. Each request is the complete charge set of one independently quoted monthly statement; caps apply within that set. Collections may be empty. Lexicographic ID order = Unicode code-point order. Do not add response keys beyond those specified.

Credit rules (release 1.0): uncapped credit per line = floor(charge_cents * 10 / 100), rounded down separately per line. Cap = 2400 cents shared by all lines with the same account_id across its subscriptions; distinct accounts have independent caps. Priority within a cap group: earliest service_on first, ties by increasing line_id. Each line gets its uncapped credit up to the group remaining cap; later lines get only the remainder or zero. total_credit = sum of assigned credits; line amount due = charge - assigned credit; total due = total charges - total credit.

quote command: {"command":"quote","line":LINE} optionally with "release":"1.0". Response has exactly release, line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents; a one-line quote treats the line as the entire statement. Unsupported release -> {"error":"unsupported_release"}.

total command (issue trial-aiw): {"command":"total","lines":[LINE,...]} optionally with "release":"1.0". Response has exactly release, credit_cents, amount_due_cents for the whole charge set; the account cap is applied across all supplied lines (not a collection of independent single-line quotes). Empty statement -> {"release":"1.0","credit_cents":0,"amount_due_cents":0}. quote remains available alongside total.

Implementation: main.py assign_credits() is the shared engine used by both quote() and total(); verified by tests/test_quote.py, tests/test_total.py, public_tests/release_1_quote.json and public_tests/release_1_total.json (all passing 2026-09-07).

memory_after.meridian-credits/release-2.0-credit-agre:
Meridian Credits release "2.0" loyalty credit agreement (Finance-approved and permanently adopted as the CURRENT agreement; source: issue trial-fxq description). Applies to quote and total with omitted release and to explicit release "2.0". Explicit release "1.0" still uses the original agreement recorded under key meridian-credits/release-1.0-credit-agreement (that record remains valid historical/explicit-release knowledge; its "omitted release selects 1.0" statement is superseded by this record). Supported releases: "1.0", "2.0"; unsupported -> {"error":"unsupported_release"}. Response release reports the agreement actually used. Request/response shapes and charge-line definition are unchanged from 1.0 (see that record). Replaces the current agreement for every supplied charge set regardless of service dates.

Credit rules (release 2.0): uncapped credit per line = floor(charge_cents * 15 / 100), rounded down separately per line. Cap = 3000 cents shared by all lines with the same (account_id, subscription_id) pair; distinct pairs (including the same subscription_id under different accounts) have independent caps. Priority within a cap group: largest charge_cents first, ties by increasing line_id (Unicode code-point order); service_on plays no role. Each line gets its uncapped credit up to the group remaining cap; later lines get only the remainder or zero. total_credit = sum of assigned credits; line amount due = charge - assigned credit; total due = total charges - total credit.

Example: quote with omitted release, charge_cents 19999 -> {"release":"2.0","credit_cents":2999,"amount_due_cents":17000,"line_id":"L-1"}. Empty total with release "2.0" -> {"release":"2.0","credit_cents":0,"amount_due_cents":0}.

Implementation: main.py RELEASES table holds rate_percent, cap_cents, group_key and priority per release; CURRENT_RELEASE = "2.0"; assign_credits(lines, release=CURRENT_RELEASE) is the shared engine for quote() and total(). Verified 2026-09-07 by tests/test_release_2.py, tests/test_quote.py, tests/test_total.py, tests/test_smoke.py and public_tests/release_1_quote.json, release_1_total.json, release_2_quote_total.json (all passing).

DESCRIPTION

  Meridian Credits quotes loyalty credits for a subscription reseller. The    
  local Python CLI accepts one JSON object on stdin and emits exactly one JSON
  object on stdout; run python3 main.py. Preserve {"command":"ping"} ->       
  {"status":"ok","product":"Meridian Credits"} and the existing unknown-      
  command response. No network, clock, locale or third-party package is       
  needed. Malformed input is outside these issues.                            
                                                                              
  A charge line has exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on, 
  and charge_cents. The three IDs are nonempty strings; line_id is unique     
  within a request. A subscription is identified by the pair (account_id,     
  subscription_id); the same subscription_id can occur under different        
  accounts, and a subscription can have several charge lines. service_on is a 
  valid Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD date from 2020-01-01 through 2099-12-31.         
  charge_cents is a nonnegative integer in US cents. No line is excluded by   
  its service date. Each request is the complete charge set of one            
  independently quoted monthly statement; caps apply within that set. Line    
  collections may be empty. Lexicographic ID order means Unicode code-point   
  order. JSON object key order is immaterial; do not add response keys beyond 
  those specified.                                                            
                                                                              
  Release "1.0" is the initial agreement. An omitted release selects the      
  current agreement; an explicit supported release selects that version.      
  Versions introduced in an issue remain supported afterward. Public suites   
  name a specific release and send explicit release values, so their          
  expectations remain applicable when the current agreement changes. Run a    
  supplied suite with python3 test_public.py --cases PATH.                    
                                                                              
  Finance has permanently adopted release 2.0 as the current agreement: Each  
  line's uncapped credit is 15% of charge_cents, rounded down separately to   
  integer cents. The 3000-cent credit cap is shared by all lines with the same
  (account_id, subscription_id) pair. Distinct groups have independent caps.  
  Within each cap group, credit is assigned to lines in this priority: largest
  charge_cents first; equal charges use increasing line_id. Each line receives
  its uncapped credit up to the group's remaining cap; later lines receive    
  only the remaining credit, or zero. The total credit is the sum of assigned 
  line credits. A line's amount due is its charge minus its assigned credit;  
  the total due is total charges minus total credit.                          
                                                                              
  Requests to quote and total with omitted release now use release "2.0".     
  Support explicit release "2.0" with the same behavior. Explicit release     
  "1.0" quote and total requests continue to use the original approved        
  agreement. Request/response shapes are unchanged; the response release      
  identifies the agreement actually used. This replaces the current agreement 
  for every supplied charge set, regardless of service dates.
